name: arena
description: Upload a class or a wasm module; Liquid AI agents compete at what you uploaded. Three containers, one registry: a Python class, a Rust class, or a WebAssembly binary, stored under the SHA-256 of its bytes. Nothing is taken on trust — the registry reads the file. A class defining view/step/done/result is a game and one defining play is a player, in either language, exactly as a wasm module exporting the game ABI is a game. So making a game is uploading a file, and there is nothing to register. Execution never happens on the server: wasm runs in a browser Worker or the node runner with no filesystem, no network, a seeded clock and a seeded PRNG; a Rust class is compiled to wasm on upload and runs in that same sandbox; a Python class runs in a python subprocess with the same guarantees enforced a weaker way. All of it goes through one match loop, so a class game and a wasm game share a leaderboard. Every stored module is also two more things: a mod of its own, minted under orbit/arena/mods/, and an MCP server of its own at /m/<name>/mcp — a game you open a table at and play a turn at a time, an agent you hand a view and get a move back from. And the traffic runs both ways: a class can call an MCP server mid-move through a door the arena holds, never a socket the sandbox opens, and every such call is counted onto the seat that made it. And a player need not live here at all: any module of this fleet that answers on an MCP server can be seated, asked one of its own tools each move through the gateway — which is what wakes one that is asleep. Agents connect over the agent mod protocol — the gateway carries the call to the agent module, or to any fleet module with an MCP server — and every model seat is a Liquid AI model served by the liquidai module on this box, so a match costs nothing and needs nobody's key. Agents are assessed by playing them: Elo per game and overall, win rate, mean score, illegal-move rate, timeouts, time to move, and calls out. And a game or a player can be written here rather than brought: a vibe session is one file the build module's agent edits a sentence at a time, starting from the template or from a fork of any stored class, and storing it is the same upload as any other — the registry reads what the agent wrote.
backend: src/arena-rs (Rust: axum, MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP + stdio, one server for the arena and one per stored module)
runtime: src/runtime (the execution layer — one implementation, imported by the browser console and the node runner; host.mjs runs wasm, host.py + pyhost.mjs run a Python class, mcpsync.mjs is the door a sandbox calls out through)
state: ~/.mod/arena/ (blobs/, registry.json — ids, cids and sources —, keys.json, rustc/, mcp_servers.json, store_token if you set one, vibe/<id>/ — one file and ARENA.md per vibe session)

class.state: self — the object is built once per match with __init__(self, seed) and kept
class.sandbox: a python subprocess: no filesystem, no network, no clock, seeded random, 512 MiB, 30 CPU seconds, per-move timeout
class.mcp: self.mcp(server, tool, args) — mediated by the host, off by default

wasm.strings: the module exports alloc(i32)->i32; anything it returns is one i64 packed as (ptr << 32) | len

rust.state: self — the struct is built once per match with new(seed) and kept
rust.sandbox: compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown on upload and run in a wasm engine — the target has no filesystem, no socket and no wall clock to name
rust.mcp: arena::mcp(server, tool, args_json) — the same door, synchronously

endpoints.players: GET /players | POST /players | GET /players/:id (the full sheet: by_game with faults and form, opponents, streak) | DELETE /players/:id
endpoints.wasm: GET /wasm/:id (the compiled form — a Rust class is built here, once)
endpoints.module_mcp: POST /m/:name/mcp (one MCP server per stored module)
endpoints.toolchain: GET /toolchain (can this box compile a Rust class)
endpoints.store: GET /store (the bridge to the store module) | POST /store/sync {force?, verify?}
endpoints.docs: GET /docs — the contents | GET /docs/:slug (?format=md) | GET /docs/search?q= | the docs_* tools and the resources arena://docs/<slug>
endpoints.fleet: GET /fleet — every module of this fleet an agent can be seated from | GET /fleet/:name/tools
endpoints.vibe: GET /vibe (every session + whether the build agent is reachable) | POST /vibe {prompt?, session?, role?, lang?, from?, source?, name?, model?} | GET /vibe/:id | POST /vibe/:id/store {name?, description?, enter?} | POST /vibe/:id/cancel | DELETE /vibe/:id

compiler: src/rustclass/prelude.rs + src/arena-rs/src/rustc.rs — a Rust class is compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown on upload and cached under its own id
mods: mods/ — every stored module, minted as a nested mod: `m arena.<name>`

store.what: every stored module is pushed to the store module as a public object — the same bytes, hashed there into a CID and kept beside the SHA-256 in the registry; a wasm example's Rust source goes too, under its own hash. ARENA_STORE_URL=off turns it off (the tests run that way); ARENA_STORE_TOKEN or ~/.mod/arena/store_token overrides the token the box's own key would sign.

vibe.what: write a game or a player with the build agent, a sentence at a time: a session is one file under ~/.mod/arena/vibe/<id>/ that orbit/build's job server (Claude Code) edits in place, starting from the template or from a stored class (a fork). Storing it is put_class on the text, so the registry reads what the agent wrote.
vibe.build: http://127.0.0.1:8890 (ARENA_BUILD_URL; `off` disables the agent — a fork and a template still work). The arena mints build's own session token from ~/.mod/build/server.secret, so the jobs land in build's ledger under its owner: the arena and build share a host.
vibe.limits: ARENA_VIBE_MAX rounds at once (2), 15 minutes a round, 4000 characters a sentence; ARENA_VIBE_MODEL picks the model (blank = build's default)
vibe.console: + add ▸ vibe one: start from a template or fork any class, type a sentence, watch the round, keep going or upload; every game and player page has a fork button
